answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The pearl multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and tundra lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3774 identities would post 2084 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
